cases.name: trap-error-catches
cases.doc: a failing primitive (head of empty list) must produce a CATCHABLE error on every impl; the handler returns CAUGHT

cases.name: trap-error-message
cases.doc: user (simple-error ...) is catchable and error-to-string recovers the message identically everywhere. Eval print is unquoted, so S42 C/Forth agree with the Go golden (boom not "boom").

cases.name: error-message-head
cases.doc: the kernel error MESSAGE for (head []) should agree across impls on the same kernel. S41.2 is 'head expects a non-empty list'; S42 sys.kl includes a trailing newline in the kernel string. Combined shen-go (41.2) vs shen-c/shen-forth (42) may FAIL — that is a kernel split, not a quoting bug.

cases.name: int-div-zero
cases.doc: RESOLVED (was a known divergence): (/ 1 0) now raises a CATCHABLE kernel error on every impl, so the handler yields 'divide-by-zero' everywhere. Previously shen-go did NOT raise -- (/ 1 0) returned maxint (9223372036854775807); the shen-go fix (fix-go-divzero-and-floatfmt) converged this. Now asserted as a HARD agreement: any impl that fails to raise (e.g. returns maxint) is a real FAIL.
